[Turn 3] The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, is a significant center for botanical research, education, and conservation. It plays a crucial role in understanding the world's plant diversity and its importance to human health, agriculture, and the environment. One of the key areas of research at Kew is the study of toxic plants, which can provide valuable insights into natural products and their potential applications in medicine and other fields.
